Flow.description:
Fundraising Quick Start: fires synchronously when a GiftDefaultDesignation whose parent is a GiftCommitment is inserted, or when an existing GDD has its ParentRecordId or GiftDesignationId change, and delegates to FQS_Recalculate_GC_FulfillmentType. Runs in the caller transaction so the recalculated FulfillmentType lands in the same commit.
Bulkification: bypassed for callers who hold the FQS_Bypass_Automation custom permission (assigned via the FQS Bypass Automation permset). Data-migration and Data Loader jobs should assume that permset for their running user so multi-thousand-record inserts/updates don't multiply this flow's work into their transaction. After migration, run scripts/apex/fqs-recalc-gc-fulfillmenttype.apex to bring FulfillmentType current on every GC.
GDD.ParentRecordId is polymorphic across Campaign / GC / Opportunity. The parent-type gate lives in the `<filterFormula>` on start (LEFT(ParentRecordId,3) = '6gc'), so Campaign and Opportunity parents never enter the flow at all — cheaper than a Decision element to a dead end.
Formula-field gap: GDD.FQS_Restriction_Type__c mirrors parent GD.FQS_Restriction_Type__c; ISCHANGED on a formula field doesn't fire reliably in Flow, so re-classifying the parent GD only propagates to child GC FulfillmentTypes when a GDD itself is re-saved. If it becomes a real gap, add a GD AfterSave flow that ISCHANGED({!$Record.FQS_Restriction_Type__c}) → loops over child GDDs and calls this subflow.
Rule (implemented in the subflow): Conditional if any child GDD has FQS_Restriction_Type__c NOT equal to "Without Donor Restriction" OR FQS_Restriction_Release_Date__c is populated; otherwise Unconditional. Subflow is idempotent — no recursion risk.
Reparenting caveat: this flow recalcs the NEW parent GC when ParentRecordId changes. The OLD parent's FulfillmentType drifts until something else on it re-triggers the recalc — acceptable because GDDs almost never move between parents in practice.
Flow.label: FQS GC Fulfillment From GDD
